newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stks close ahead a tad, led by Electricidad.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stks close ahead a tad, led by Electricidad.

text.p: Caracas stocks closed ahead a hair in strong trade, led by leading utility Electricidad de Caracas, brokers said.

"It was a busy session with electricity shares well bid after being knocked back for so long by the labor protests," said Vencred broker Geronimo Paolini. Spanish bank Santander rated Electricidad a "buy" in a research note released Friday.
The bolsa's 19-share index edged ahead 0.22 percent to close at 6,407.68 points as 46 million shares traded, worth 5.9 billion boivars ($12.5 million).

Foods company Mavesa dropped 4.25 bolivars to close at 153.50 on investor unease after a shareholder, who owns 0.0003 percent of the company, asked Venezuela's Securities Commission (CNV) to suspend the stock.
The shareholder has said Mavesa approved company results on Wednesday's general meeting that did not include damages from a possible six billion bolivar legal suit.

But Mavesa denied the claim, and in a press release said it had approved the results on the basis of advice from independent auditors and had always maintained transparency in its dealings with both the CNV and investors.
Among traded stocks 21 rose, 11 fell and 11 closed flat.
Volume was boosted as nearly 30 million Corimon B shares cross traded, the stock closing off 0.1 bolivars at 9.00.

However, traders did not see Friday's session's rise as heralding the start of a rally. "Apart from Electricidad nothing much was moving today, and I don't see anything moving much over the short term either," said one.
